raw.assessment: The incumbent offers a repeatable conversational routine and printed access; seven frequent attendees explicitly found repetition helpful. This supports retaining the structure, although it does not establish its causal benefit. The concrete limiting observation is five occasional attendees struggling to enter conversations already familiar to partners: continuity may help some while creating an entry burden for others. Reported useful speaking reached 49/72 slips and correct preparation identification 48/72; missing responses, unlinked slips and untimed speaking limit interpretation. Coordination ranged across the 90-minute ceiling. Neither these data nor slow pair formation alone establish proficiency mismatch as the cause.

openings.claim: Prior-conversation familiarity may impede entry independently of proficiency. A standalone first exchange, with each partner briefly establishing the shared context and taking an initial turn, could retain the familiar session structure while easing entry.
openings.delta: Change only the start of paired practice using existing printed prompts; no attendance prerequisite or public proficiency label.
openings.prediction: If shared-context deficits matter, fewer participants will report being unable to enter an already-familiar conversation and useful-speaking reports will improve even when pair-formation duration remains similar.
openings.probe: Across six sessions, alternate pairs between the existing opening and the standalone exchange. Observe formation duration and first reciprocal exchange separately; collect anonymous entry-difficulty and useful-speaking reports. Record preparation effort within weekly coordination totals.
assumptions: The exchange replaces existing practice time within 75 minutes.
Prompts permit entry without prior attendance.
Optional anonymous feedback can distinguish prior topic familiarity without public labels.

openings.claim: Some preparation errors may reflect confusion between successive task sheets. A consistent printed panel identifying the next Wednesday's date and one conversational preparation action may improve task recognition.
openings.delta: Add explicit session identity to the existing paper channel; keep participation possible without completing preparation.
openings.prediction: Earlier-task answers will decline specifically; unchanged blank answers would suggest an additional access, attention or comprehension problem.
openings.probe: Use the panel for six sessions and tally correct, earlier and blank answers separately, alongside printing and message-answering minutes. Keep current and next preparation sheets available in the room for anyone attending, including newcomers.
assumptions: Date ambiguity contributes to earlier-task answers.
A reusable panel adds little preparation work.

raw.assessment: The stipulated observations support difficulty entering conversations and identifying preparation, but establish neither proficiency mismatch nor the causes of lost practice. Useful speaking time and coordination savings remain unverified. Two bounded paper-based capabilities could be tested within ordinary sessions.

openings.claim: A speculative self-adjusting conversation sheet could let partners begin a useful exchange without shared attendance history or public proficiency labels. It would combine a fresh shared scenario, optional sentence supports and extension prompts, and alternating speaker turns.
openings.delta: Dependencies are understandable support choices, prompts that work independently of prior sessions, partners accepting different supports, and balanced turns that still feel useful. The presently testable partial capability is a printed scenario with optional supports; participants select or change supports without declaring a level.
openings.prediction: If missing shared context constrains entry, fresh scenarios should shorten first-exchange latency. If support mismatch matters separately, optional supports should increase useful speaking reports even with fresh scenarios held constant.
openings.probe: Within existing practice time, counterbalance short rounds using fresh versus familiar scenarios and optional versus existing supports. Observe first-exchange latency and individual speaking minutes; collect anonymous usefulness reports. Keep the familiar opening ritual. Across six sessions, count all attendances in the 80% reporting target and log total volunteer minutes against the under-90-minute limit, including preparation of variants.
assumptions: Participants can use support options without public proficiency labels.
Observation and printing fit existing volunteer capacity; this must be measured.
Timed speech alone does not establish usefulness.

openings.claim: Would a conspicuously dated paper preparation panel prevent obsolete-task selection, or do participants need clearer task wording even when viewing the correct sheet?
openings.delta: A future paper system that always exposes the current task depends on version recognition, comprehensible wording and a route for missed-session arrivals. Test version recognition first rather than assuming messaging access is the cause.
openings.prediction: If version confusion dominates, date emphasis should reduce earlier-task answers. Persisting errors while the correct panel is visible would implicate comprehension or attention instead.
openings.probe: Compare ordinary and date-emphasized printed panels with identical task wording; ask participants to identify the next task with papers visible and again at exit. Give missed-session arrivals the current panel and allow participation without preparation. Track the 85% identification target and printing time.
assumptions: Printed panels remain available at every session.
Date recognition is accessible to participants; neither smartphones nor accounts are required.

openings.claim: Shared-context deficits may impede entry independently of proficiency; fresh standalone scenarios with reciprocal initial turns may help. Optional sentence supports and extensions address a separate possible support mismatch.
openings.discriminator: Context help should reduce entry difficulty or first-exchange latency even without faster pairing; support benefits should persist with fresh context held constant.
openings.fit: Preserve familiar ritual; replace practice within 75 minutes; permit attendance gaps and private, changeable support choices.
openings.probe: Across six sessions counterbalance existing versus standalone contextual exchanges and existing versus optional supports. Observe pairing duration, first exchange and individual speaking minutes separately; collect anonymous entry difficulty, prior familiarity and usefulness reports. Include variant preparation in total volunteer minutes.
openings.uncertainty: Shared-context, support and turn-balance mechanisms remain hypotheses; bundled context/turn changes cannot isolate each. Support comprehension, partner acceptance and volunteer capacity are unverified; timed speech is not usefulness.

openings.claim: A reusable printed panel naming next Wednesday and one conversational action may reduce obsolete-task selection; wording comprehension, attention and access remain distinct possibilities.
openings.discriminator: Fewer earlier-task answers support version confusion; persistent errors with the correct sheet visible suggest comprehension or attention. Blanks may have additional causes.
openings.fit: Keep current/next sheets available offline, including missed-session arrivals; preparation is optional.
openings.probe: Compare ordinary versus date-emphasized panels with identical wording over six sessions. Ask with papers visible and at exit; tally correct, earlier and blank answers; log printing and message-answering minutes.
openings.uncertainty: Date ambiguity, accessible date recognition and low template effort are assumptions.

lineage.reason: Optional supports and reciprocal turns remain explicit.
Version recognition and blank-response distinction retained.

post_distill.decision: Test both provisionally: free conversational practice, one room, no paid time, public labels or digital requirement. Across all attendances assess 80% reporting ten useful minutes, 85% identifying preparation and under 90 weekly coordination minutes. Stipulated, unlinked, incomplete self-reports establish no causal benefit.
